questions.def: 'It' is used as a dummy subject when the real subject is an infinitive.
questions.question: ___ is important to consider all options before deciding.

questions.def: 'There' introduces a statement about the existence of something.
questions.question: ___ appears to be a mistake in the calculations.

questions.def: 'There seems' is used to introduce an apparent problem.
questions.question: ___ to be a problem with the connection.

questions.def: 'There is' indicates the absence of a reason or purpose.
questions.question: ___ is no point in arguing about it now.

questions.def: 'It is believed' introduces a generally held opinion or belief.
questions.question: ___ is believed that the suspect has fled the country.

questions.def: Should be 'It is vital' because 'to maintain' is the real subject.
questions.question: There is vital to maintain a positive attitude.

questions.def: 'It appears' introduces an observation or impression.
questions.question: ___ that the meeting will be postponed.

questions.def: 'It' is the dummy subject; 'to admit' is the real subject.
questions.question: ___ takes courage to admit when you're wrong.

questions.def: 'There are' introduces a list or quantity of things.
questions.question: ___ are several factors contributing to the problem.

questions.def: 'It happened' introduces an event or occurrence.
questions.question: ___ that I saw her yesterday.

questions.def: 'It' is used as a dummy subject for infinitives ('to practice').
questions.question: ___ is essential to practice regularly.

questions.def: 'There is' indicates the existence of something (probability).
questions.question: ___ is a high probability of rain tomorrow.

questions.def: 'It' is needed to introduce the belief; 'It is believed'.
questions.question: There is believed to be some truth in it.

questions.def: 'There is' introduces the absence of an easy solution.
questions.question: ___ no easy solution to this problem.

questions.def: 'It seems' introduces an opinion or assessment.
questions.question: ___ seems unlikely that he will accept the offer.

questions.def: 'There were' indicates the quantity of people present.
questions.question: ___ were only a few people at the meeting.

questions.def: 'There is' indicates the existence of a reason.
questions.question: ___ a good reason to be cautious.

questions.def: 'It' is the dummy subject, and 'to complete' is the real subject.
questions.question: ___ is necessary to complete the task on time.

questions.def: 'There remained' indicates the remaining quantity of questions.
questions.question: ___ remained several unanswered questions.

questions.def: 'There is' indicates the absence of doubt.
questions.question: ___ no doubt that he will succeed.

questions.def: 'It' refers to the distance; 'to go' is the real subject.
questions.question: ___ is a long way to go before we reach the top.

questions.def: 'There exist' introduces theories on a subject.
questions.question: ___ exist several theories on this subject.

questions.def: 'It seems' introduces a feeling or impression about something.
questions.question: ___ that she is telling the truth.

questions.def: 'It' is a dummy subject; 'considering' is the gerund phrase.
questions.question: ___ is worth considering the alternative options.

questions.def: 'There is' introduces the likelihood of delays.
questions.question: ___ is likely to be delays due to the weather.

questions.def: Dummy 'it' introduces a general fact/situation, postponing the real subject.
questions.question: ___ is crucial to double-check all figures before submission.

questions.def: 'There' introduces the existence of something: a misunderstanding.
questions.question: ___ appears to be a misunderstanding regarding the new policy.

questions.def: 'There seems' introduces something that exists, agreeing with singular 'seems'.
questions.question: ___ to be some confusion about the schedule changes.

questions.def: 'It' introduces impersonal passive constructions ('it is believed').
questions.question: ___ is believed that the suspect has left the country.

questions.def: Dummy 'it' introduces a difficult task/action, postponing real subject.
questions.question: ___ wasn't easy to find a parking space downtown.
